subject: Solace - shoulder reserve and autoscale proposal
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solace - shoulder reserve and autoscale proposal

Adam / Erin —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, I pulled together a lightweight proposal for how we can structure Dedicated capacity for Solace with a small "shoulder reserve" to protect you during episodic traffic bursts (clinical batch jobs + nightly inference windows). The goal: keep predictable SLAs for peak traffic without forcing you to overcommit on reserved GPUs.

High-level proposal (attached calc):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 x A100-equivalent for sustained throughput (covers 95% of observed minutes)
- Shoulder reserve: +3 ephemeral GPUs (warmed and standing by) that can attach within 60s when queue depth spikes above threshold
- Autoscale policy: progressive scale up in steps (1 GPU increments) with a max of 12 total, scale down guarded by a 10-minute grace to avoid thrash
- Pricing note: shoulder reserve billed as lower-commitment reserved slab (discounted compared to pure on-demand), ephemeral bursts billed at usage rate

Attached I included the headroom calculation and a sample traffic profile you shared. Dev has a recommended autoscale ruleset that maps queue percentiles -> actions; I cc'd him for the technical details.

Next step: quick 30-min alignment to lock thresholds and acceptable attach latency. Are you available tomorrow at 10am PT?

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Thanks Markus — this looks helpful and aligned with what we sketched. A few clarifying Qs from our infra team: 

1) What do you guarantee around attach latency for the shoulder reserve? We need <90s for some of the nightly pipelines.
2) If we hit the 12 GPU hard cap, is there an automated fallback (e.g., degrade to lower quantized model) or routing to hosted?
3) How is billing handled during rapid scale-up/scale-down cycles — do you bill per-second/minute?

Erin, any constraints I’ve missed? Happy to join the sync tomorrow.

—Adam

adam.chen@solacetherapeutics.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Adam Chen <adam.chen@solacetherapeutics.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Erin Morales <erin@solacetherapeutics.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solace - shoulder reserve and autoscale proposal

Adam — quick answers and technical notes below. I attached a sample autoscale rule JSON.

1) Attach latency: with warmed images and a pre-staged kv-cache we can target 45–75s median for attaching one GPU from the shoulder reserve. Cold attach could be 120–180s; we recommend keeping the reserve standing ready.
2) Fallback: yes — we can wire a policy to fallback to a quantized 8-bit model or route lowest-priority traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints in a different region. I added a policy snippet: 
   - If queue wait > 60s and total_gpus == max, then route non-critical requests to hosted (region fallback) and send alert to the on-call.
3) Billing cadence: Dedicated burst usage is billed per-minute with 1-minute granularity for ephemeral GPUs. Shoulder reserve has a blended hourly reservation rate (smaller commitment) plus usage spikes billed per-minute.

I also included recommended hysteresis: only scale down if utilization < 30% for 10m, and immediate scale-up if queue > 60% for 2 consecutive 60s windows.

Attaching: sample_traffic_profiles.json, autoscale_policy_example.json

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
Attachment: autoscale_policy_example.json (policy snippet)

Looping Lauren for commercial confirmation before we confirm pricing with Solace. Short note: recommend the blended shoulder slab at 30% discount to on-demand, ephemeral bursts at standard dedicated burst rate. We should keep reserve attachment SLA (<=90s) in the amendment.

Also flagging margin impact: if they keep 3 GPUs warm 24/7 we need to price the slab accordingly so it doesn’t erode committed revenue targets for Q2. Can you run a quick margin calc and confirm acceptable discount bands?

—Markus
